title: 42 Lakh LIC Claim Recovery for Retired Teacher in Malleshwaram
subtitle: Rejected for pre-existing disease disclosure. We filed an appeal with medical records and got the full claim approved.
author: Hari Kotian
originalDenialReason: Pre-existing disease (diabetes + hypertension) disclosed after treatment
summary: A retired school teacher's LIC health claim was rejected within 7 days of submission, citing non-disclosure of diabetes. The policy had been in force for 8 years. We analyzed the rejection letter, submitted additional medical records from 3 different hospitals spanning 3 years, and demonstrated that the diabetes was a known but controlled condition, not newly developed. The claim was approved in full within 42 days.
situation: 58-year-old retired school teacher from Malleshwaram had a pre-existing diabetes diagnosis for 5 years. LIC rejected the claim citing material non-disclosure — diabetes was mentioned in one hospital record but not all.
task: Demonstrate that the diabetes was properly disclosed across relevant medical records, not selectively omitted. Prove the rejection was based on an incomplete medical review, not fraud.
action: Collected 3 years of medical records from 4 different hospitals
Cross-referenced with the original proposal form — diabetes was listed under existing conditions
Drafted a 15-page appeal letter citing IRDAI Health Insurance Regulations 2016
Built a timeline showing no symptoms or treatments were hidden
Escalated to the GRO with specific reference to IRDAI regulations
resultDetails: LIC's GRO reviewed the case within 12 days and approved the full claim. The approval letter cited incomplete initial review as the reason for reversal.
lessons: Insurers must review ALL available medical records
A well-drafted appeal with proper regulation references gets faster responses
clientQuote: I was devastated when LIC rejected the claim. Hari Kotian Sir analyzed 3 years of my medical files and found that LIC's own doctor had only looked at one hospital's records. Within 6 weeks, the full amount was in my account.
consultationCta: Do you have a rejected claim in Bangalore? Get a free 15-minute audit of your rejection letter.

seo.metaDescription: Read how we recovered 42.85 lakh for a retired teacher whose LIC claim was rejected for pre-existing disease disclosure.

title: Getting 18 Lakh Health Claim Approved After 365-Day Delay
subtitle: Max Bupa delayed payment for over a year. We intervened and got it settled within 14 days.
author: Hari Kotian
summary: A small business owner's 18.5 lakh health claim for his father's cardiac surgery was stuck in document verification for 365 days. Max Bupa requested the same documents 4 times. We filed an IRDAI IGMS complaint, escalated to the Ombudsman, and got the full amount plus 8 percent interest within 14 days.
situation: Business owner from Rajajinagar submitted a health claim after his father's bypass surgery. Max Bupa kept asking for additional documents — same ones already submitted. No status updates for 365 days.
task: Break the documentation loop and force a resolution through regulatory channels.
action: Mapped every document submitted over 365 days
Filed IRDAI IGMS complaint with evidence of the documentation loop
Notified Max Bupa GRO that the case was on IGMS
Within 48 hours of IGMS filing, Max Bupa's claims head called to settle
Negotiated for interest at 8 percent per annum
resultDetails: Settlement of 18,50,000 plus 1,48,000 interest within 14 days of filing the IGMS complaint.
lessons: 60+ days of delay is a valid IGMS complaint
Document everything with dates and reference numbers
IRDAI IGMS works — insurers respond within 48 hours
Interest is recoverable on delayed claims
clientQuote: I was sending the same medical reports month after month for a year. When I complained to IRDAI, Max Bupa called me within 2 days. They paid the claim and interest within 2 weeks.
consultationCta: Has your insurer delayed your claim for 60+ days? File an IGMS complaint — I'll help you draft it for free.

seo.metaDescription: How we got an 18.5 lakh Max Bupa claim settled with interest after 365 days of delay.
